PEACOCK Intelligence Engine

Numerical AI primitives with honest scale limits.

A small, testable CPU foundation for tensors, autodiff, neural-network training, evaluation and inference.

What the Intelligence Engine verifies

The current engine is independently implemented in the repository and uses CPU-only Python numerical kernels.

CPU · tested

Tensor algebra

Shape-aware tensors, indexing, reductions, broadcasting, rank-2 matmul, activations (ReLU, GELU, Sigmoid, Tanh), LayerNorm, cosine similarity and stable softmax.

Reverse mode

Automatic differentiation

A local computation graph accumulates gradients; central finite-difference checks verify Dense, matmul, softmax, GELU and LayerNorm backward passes.

Small models

Training

Dense/Sequential models, XOR and spiral datasets, MSE/cross-entropy, SGD/Adam and evaluation metrics.

Custom artifacts

Inference and save/load

Small-model inference and .pkm serialization/quantisation helpers exist; no production model-serving target.

Executable AI examples

The site embeds the current source files at build time; it does not invent benchmark results.

examples/tensors.pac

Selectable source — use your browser's copy command. · SHA-256: 8b7195600c448d89

// Differentiable computation in PEACOCK: matmul, loss, reverse-mode gradients.
module tensors

use nn

fn main() -> Unit {
    capability compute;

    let x = tensor([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]]);
    let column = tensor([[0.5], [1.5]]);
    let projected = x.matmul(column);
    print("matmul: " + str(projected));
    print("shape: " + str(projected.shape));
    print("softmax: " + str(tensor([[1.0, 2.0, 3.0]]).softmax()));

    let weights = nn.parameter([[0.1, -0.2], [0.3, 0.4]]);
    let targets = tensor([[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0]]);
    let predictions = x.matmul(weights);
    let loss = nn.mse(predictions, targets);
    print("loss: " + str(loss.item()));
    loss.backward();
    print("weight gradient: " + str(weights.grad));

    // Analytic check: for mean-squared error, dL/dW = X^T * (2/N) * (P - T).
    let expected = x.transpose().matmul((predictions - targets) * 0.5);
    print("autodiff gradient: " + str(weights.grad));
    print("closed-form gradient: " + str(expected));
    print("max abs difference: " + str(nn.max_abs_diff(weights.grad, expected)));
}

examples/xor.pac

Selectable source — use your browser's copy command. · SHA-256: 1af124d491c4d489

// Train a small neural network on XOR, entirely through PEACOCK syntax.
module xor_net

use nn

model XorNet {
    input x: Tensor<Float32, [2]>
    output y: Tensor<Float32, [2]>
    stack {
        Dense(units: 8, activation: relu)
        Dense(units: 2)
    }
}

training XorTraining {
    objective: "cross_entropy"
    optimiser: "adam"
    epochs: 400
    learning_rate: 0.05
    batch_size: 4
    seed: 7
}

fn main() -> Unit {
    capability compute;
    let data = nn.xor();
    let net = XorNet.init(seed: 7);
    let losses = XorTraining.run(net, data);
    let accuracy = XorTraining.evaluate(net, data);
    print("epochs: " + str(len(losses)));
    print("final loss: " + str(nn.loss(net, data, loss: "cross_entropy")));
    print("accuracy: " + str(accuracy));
}

No GPU, accelerator backend, frontier-scale training, attention stack or mobile inference backend is verified in this checkout.
